First Record of the Goby Lentipes armatus Sakai and Nakamura, 1979 (Teleostei: Gobiidae) in the Amburayan River in Benguet, Luzon Island, Philippines. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 29(1), 78–81. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/29.1.2020C0015
source.sourceReview: Official NFRDI article metadata and indexed full-text/PDF excerpts were reviewed. Direct page/PDF retrieval timed out in the web reader, so exact content access was limited to those official indexed excerpts; no local PDF, sequence file, voucher catalog or raw dataset was retained.

publication.journalPolicyLicense: CC BY-NC 4.0, as stated in the journal-wide copyright and permissions policy
publication.reuseDisposition: Keep the article as a research citation and use only concise attributed factual summaries. Do not reproduce article text, tables or specimen photographs. The noncommercial license does not authorize an app distribution or commercial use without confirming Bangwit use terms.

study.waterbody: Amburayan River, Benguet, Cordillera Administrative Region

landedCatchSamplingSitesInMethods.evidence: The methods state that enumerators collected landed-catch specimens at this monitored landing site.
The methods state that enumerators collected landed-catch specimens at this monitored landing site.

reportedButNoLandedCatch.evidence: An NSAP enumerator documented the species at this assignment, but the article explicitly says no landed catch was reported from the Badeo landing site and the study samples came from Naguey and Cuba.

study.abstractScopeVsMethods: The abstract broadly describes photographic and actual specimens from landed-catch surveys in Atok, Kapangan and Kibungan. The detailed methods narrow the actual collected specimens to Naguey/Atok and Cuba/Kapangan, while Badeo/Kibungan had an enumerator report but no landed catch. Use the methods-level distinction; do not assign a catch specimen to Kibungan.

identificationEvidence.dnaPreservationAsReported: Two specimens were preserved in 95% ethanol and sent to the NFRDI Genetic Fingerprinting Laboratory.
identificationEvidence.dnaResultAsReported: The article reports a monophyletic Neighbor-Joining cluster with 100% bootstrap support and 0.5% and 0.7% distances between the two study sequences and reference Lentipes armatus sequences, below the paper's cited 3.0–3.5% delineation threshold.
identificationEvidence.interpretation: This is stronger local identification evidence than the name-only entry in the 2018 survey, but the reviewed material does not provide a museum voucher catalog number or a separately linked raw sequence accession for the two samples. Treat the molecular result as reported by the article, not independently reanalyzed here.

spatialLimits: The reviewed article provides barangay/municipality landing-site names but no site coordinates or station-level GIS file.
Do not derive river geometry or a precise point from locality names.

sourceDateConflict.methodsDate: The methods state specimens were collected September 1–10, 2015.
sourceDateConflict.figureCaptionDate: The Figure 2 caption describes the photographed male and female specimens as caught in Amburayan River in 2018.
sourceDateConflict.disposition: Unresolved in the reviewed text. Do not assume the figure specimens are the same individuals or collection batch as the 2015 methods samples.

crossSourceConflict.earlierSource: Garcia et al. (2018), Assessment of the Diversity of Macro Aquatic Species in Amburayan River in Kapangan, Benguet in the Philippines, already lists Lentipes armatus and reports 18 individuals for its 2014-12 to 2015-02 survey.
crossSourceConflict.laterSourceClaim: Tauli et al. (2022) titles the paper as a first record in Amburayan and states it is the first record in the Cordillera, while referencing Garcia et al. (2018) in its introduction.
crossSourceConflict.interpretation: The 2022 paper supplies a later, morphometric/meristic and DNA-supported local identification, but its first-record wording is not reconciled with the earlier published species list. The papers share Garcia as a coauthor and an Amburayan/NSAP research context, so they are not treated as independent corroboration. The 2018 taxon entry itself lacked the DNA confirmation described in 2022; that does not prove the source's older specimens were misidentified or identical to the later samples.

catalogContext: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes brief distribution summary did not list Benguet, but the later NFRDI paper reports a local DNA-supported identification. The catalog summary is not a complete range polygon; this paper resolves the earlier locality anomaly as a literature-backed historical record, subject to the source conflicts and reuse hold above.

disposition.historicalLocalIdentificationEvidence: Supported by a 2022 NFRDI/BFAR-CAR publication describing morphology, meristics and DNA validation from two Amburayan River samples; detailed methods locate landed samples at Naguey, Atok and Cuba, Kapangan.
disposition.reason: Historical site-specific evidence is available, but method/caption dates conflict, first-record wording conflicts with the 2018 source, exact coordinates and public vouchers are not available in the reviewed text, and the journal policy is noncommercial-only. No public app claim is admitted pending rights and source-conflict review.

nextAction: Preserve this as a historical, research-only local identification source. If a publication/author clarification is later obtained, resolve the 2015 methods versus 2018 figure-caption date and the first-record wording; keep Badeo/Kibungan as reported observation only with no landed catch. Continue northern Luzon freshwater source work without deriving present-day presence from this study.
